s: The Baroque hilltop church locals just call St. Fuma
w: Rovinj's skyline is crowned by this Baroque church at the summit of the old town, known to locals simply as St. Fuma. Guidebooks and visitors alike call it the Basilica of St. Euphemia, though it has never formally held the rank of basilica minor - grandeur has outrun the paperwork.
_facts: Baroque church on the hilltop at the heart of Rovinj's old town
Popularly called the Basilica of St. Euphemia and locally 'St. Fuma', though not formally a basilica minor

s: Red Island is really two islets joined by an embankment
w: Red Island, as its Croatian name translates, is really twins: the islet of Sveti Andrija and its smaller neighbour Maskin, joined by a man-made embankment just off Rovinj. Together the pair cover barely a quarter of a square kilometre of the Adriatic, a short boat ride from the old town.
_facts: Twinned island off Rovinj joining Sveti Andrija (St. Andrew) and the islet of Maskin via an embankment

s: A Bronze Age hillfort outside the old town
w: Long before Rovinj was Venetian, this hillfort above the town was a fortified Bronze Age settlement, occupied roughly 1850 to 1450 BC. It ranks among Istria's most significant prehistoric sites - three centuries and a half a millennium of history hiding in the scrub outside the old walls.
_facts: Bronze Age hillfort near Rovinj in Istria, occupied c. 1850/1750-1500/1450 BC

s: A cave dug since the 1800s hid its paintings until 2010
w: Excavated since the late 19th century, this Istrian cave kept a secret from every dig until 2010: cave paintings, later confirmed as the oldest known in southeast Europe and published in the journal Antiquity in 2019. Traces of Upper Paleolithic human and animal habitation remain inside.
_facts: Cave in western Istria County, excavated since the late 19th century
Contains the oldest known cave paintings in southeast Europe, discovered in 2010 by Prof. Darko Komso, published in Antiquity in 2019
Also holds Upper Paleolithic traces of human and animal habitation

s: A Turk and a Venetian glare at each other overhead
w: Built in 1678-79 on the site of Rovinj's old town gate, this arch carries carved heads on each face - a Turk on one side, a Venetian on the other - glaring past each other above the passage through to Grisia, the old town's steep artists' lane.
_facts: Arch in Rovinj's old town, built 1678-79 on the site of the former town gate
Leads to Grisia Street; carved heads of a Turk and a Venetian face opposite directions
